title: Radiation therapy: how a course goes
what: A machine directs precisely planned beams at the tumor. A session is short and painless, and a course lasts several weeks.
why: For cancer, either alone or together with surgery and chemotherapy.
duration: a session usually takes 10 to 30 minutes, with the beam on for only a few minutes; a course lasts from a few days to 6 to 8 weeks
tell_doctor: A pacemaker or other device in your body
Pregnancy, or if you could be pregnant
If you have had radiation before
If it is hard for you to lie still or in one position

prepare.title: Marking
prepare.text: Before the course, a planning CT scan is done and marks are put on your skin. Do not wash them off.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Care for the skin in the treated area as your doctor says. Do not put your own creams on it unless allowed.

steps: You change and lie on the table
You are placed in the same position using the marks, sometimes with a mask or a support
The staff leave the room but can see and hear you
The machine moves around you and sometimes hums
The beam is on for a few minutes
After the session you go straight home
feel: You do not feel the session itself
Tiredness builds up toward the middle of the course
The skin in the treated area may turn red and peel
Other effects depend on the treated area. The doctor will explain
after: After external radiation you do not give off radiation. You can hug children
Do not skip sessions without agreeing it with your doctor
Drink water, eat well and rest
Do not rub, warm or sunbathe the treated skin
red_flags: Open sores or blisters on the treated skin
Severe pain, vomiting or diarrhea so you cannot eat or drink

faq.q: Will I be radioactive after a session?
faq.a: No. With external radiation you do not give off radiation and are not a danger to your family.
Usually yes, with warm water and a mild product. Do not rub the treated area. Check with your doctor.

reminders.text: Radiation therapy session tomorrow. Do not wash off the marks on your skin, and wear soft clothes.
